primary_sources: Software Engineering Portfolio Case Study Standards

rules.explanation: Rather than presenting projects as simple code dumps, present them as case studies detailing the problem solved, the solution approach, and technical decisions made.
rules.do: Structure each project with: Problem Statement, Technical Approach, System Architecture, and Final Outcome.
rules.dont: Do not present projects with just a title and a list of technologies without explaining why or how it was built.

rules.rule_name: Visual Architecture and Proof of Work
rules.explanation: Technical reviewers quickly grasp engineering complexity through block diagrams, system flows, and video/GIF demonstrations.
rules.do: Include system architecture schematics, flowcharts, or a short demo GIF/video showcasing the system operating live.
rules.dont: Do not rely exclusively on text descriptions without visual proof of execution or hardware/software diagrams.

rules.rule_name: Explicit Tech Stack and Role Clarification
rules.explanation: Evaluators need to know your exact contribution in team projects and the precise tools utilized.
rules.do: Explicitly list the tech stack (e.g., C++, RTOS, Streamlit, Python) and state your individual role if built with a team.
rules.dont: Do not claim team projects as purely individual work or hide the specific frameworks used.

rules.rule_name: Working Repository and Live Deployment Links
rules.explanation: Broken links or private repositories reduce trust instantly. Projects must have clickable access to source code and hosted demos.
rules.do: Provide verified, active links to the GitHub repository and deployed web app or hardware demo link.
rules.dont: Do not link to private repos or dead end '404' deployment pages.
